newsitem.title: USA: Invacare sees results below analysts views.
newsitem.headline: Invacare sees results below analysts views.

text.p: Invacare Corp said Thursday it foresees quarter-to-quarter improvement and a record year, but believes its results will be less than analysts' estimates.

Wall Street is expecting the company to report earnings of $0.37 a share in the second quarter, $0.41 a share in the third quarter and $0.48 a share in the fourth quarter, according to First Call estimates.

The maker of home medical equipment cited a temporary slowdown in sales growth and the possible effects of proposed budget cuts on purchases of its equipment. It also said dampened sales growth during the past two quarters could be a trend that continues for the balance of the year.
Invacare said European reimbursement pressures continue, particularly in Germany, and this pressure, coupled with the strong dollar, will limit European sales growth for the balance of 1997.
Nonetheless, the company said it expects a record year in 1997.

"These developments are temporary in nature, and the industry has compelling growth demographics that will allow the industry and Invacare to resume more normal growth in 1998," a company statement said.
